correctness.rationale: Direct Fourier coefficients give the operator exactly; the kernel is a convex quadratic in cos(theta). The first minimum branch is strictly concave in t and crosses zero only once before t0; the second branch is strictly convex in q=b^t with unique global minimum 1-2(1-c)c^(c/(1-c)). Strict monotonicity of c(rho) and of that minimum yields a unique amplitude threshold, and a nondegenerate time minimum yields the square-root splitting. Endpoints rho=1, t=t0, t=1 and limit t to 0+ are explicitly addressed. Checker.py numerics are supplementary, not the infinite proof.
